 2026 Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs Brazil: Team Canada Set Sights on 2027 Qualifiers
 By Francesco Tosini
 November 16, 2026
 Billie Jean King Cup 
 Team Canada 
 Cheer for Canada 
 Overview 
 It’s another road trip for Team Canada as the 2026 Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs take the squad to Vitoria, Brazil, for their November 20-21 tie against the host nation Brazil. 
 The clay-court tie will be best-of-five matches, with each match being best-of-three sets. The winner will advance to the 2027 Qualifiers, while the losing nation will compete in the three Regional Group I events next year.
 This will be the sixth-straight road tie (outside of the Finals) for Team Canada, who last played on home soil back in April 2023. Canada failed to top its 2025 Qualifiers group in Japan but returned to that stage of the competition in 2026 thanks to a successful trip to Mexico for the Play-offs. The Canucks were beaten by hosts Kazakhstan in the 2026 Qualifiers back in April and will play in the Play-offs for the second-consecutive year. 
 CLICK HERE to read more about Canada’s Qualifiers tie against Kazakhstan. 
 Schedule 
 Friday, Nov. 20: Two singles matches Matches start: 2 p.m. local time (12 p.m. ET) 
 Saturday, Nov. 21: One doubles match followed by up to two singles matches* Matches start: 1 p.m. local time (11 a.m. ET) 
 *If the result of the tie is decided, the final singles matches may not be played. 
 The Teams 
 A few Canadians will be reacquainted with one another following the nation’s 2026 Qualifiers tie in Kazakhstan.  
 Bianca Andreescu, Kayla Cross, and Ariana Arseneault will don the Maple Leaf for the second time this year, and will be joined by doubles world No. 3 Gabriela Dabrowski and 18-year-old debutant Clémence Mercier, who was nominated earlier this month. Heidi el-Tabakh is back as team captain after returning from maternity leave. 
 CLICK HERE to read about Mercier’s reaction to her first-ever nomination. 
 The hosts Brazil will have someone quite familiar to a particular member of Team Canada. Luisa Stefani, Dabrowski’s doubles partner, will be her nation’s most-decorated player with six WTA doubles titles alongside the Canadian this season.  
 In singles, Brazil don’t have a player inside the Top 250. The 260 th -ranked Laura Pigossi is Brazil’s No. 1, and will be joined by Gabriela Ce, Luiza Fullana, and 16-year-old Nauhany Vitoria Leme da Silva. Brazil are captained by Luiz Peniza. 
 Read also: Ariana Arseneault Brings Career Year into Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs 
 Canada dominates the head-to-head against Brazil at the Billie Jean King Cup. The Canucks are 12-0,  with their most recent encounter coming in 2013, when Eugenie Bouchard, Sharon Fichman, and Dabrowski secured a 2-1 victory to send Canada to the World Group II Play-offs.
 Canada, who are the second seeds in the Play-offs, are ranked No. 8 in the world. Brazil is 19 th in the world rankings.
